note: Material properties for the rows McMaster labels "Spring Steel" are taken as music wire (ASTM A228). First inferred from McMaster's own published max loads -- assuming hard-drawn A227 puts 513 of 1,523 springs above allowable stress at their own rating, music wire leaves 25 -- and since confirmed on the McMaster product page for 9657K79, which states "Steel Grade: Music-Wire Steel". The 56 springs in the 96485K series are the exception: their product pages name no steel grade, rate to 300 F where music wire and hard-drawn reach only 250 F, and run to 0.625 in wire, far beyond the range music wire is drawn in. They are taken as oil-tempered A229, the 300 F grade. Shear modulus is identical for all these grades, so rate, coil count and solid length never depend on any of it; only stress does. The 1,031 metric products carry their own per-quantity sourceUnits and do not use the "in" default above: McMaster publishes those lengths in millimetres but the max load in pounds and the spring rate in lbf per millimetre, and each is stored in the unit it was published in. Their "Spring Steel" rows are DIN 17223 wire and are taken as music wire on the same test used for the inch listing -- hard-drawn puts 22 of those 54 rows above allowable stress at their own published rating, music wire leaves none.
